title: Document evidence extraction
summary: A representative document-evidence workflow with compatible OCR capture, deterministic analysis, and one typed staged-promotion transition for directory and file outputs.

use.practicalQuestion: How can a local document-evidence workflow preserve OCR provenance and deterministic analysis while one trusted writer replaces directory or file output through a typed recovery path?
use.changedAbility: A collaborator can review captured text, reproduce ordered term evidence, and inspect one shared promotion transition that reconciles events on either side of a rename effect, restores the prior state, or returns every event, coordinate, phase, and observed occupancy for re-entry.
readers: AI collaborators implementing or reviewing evidence-extraction workflows
Technical practitioners evaluating provenance, determinism, and filesystem recovery

provenance.description: Participant-account-supported reconstruction of a 2018–2019 workflow using realistic synthetic reviewed-OCR material, with a successor filesystem mechanism derived from focused architecture convergence.
provenance.temporalScope: The account describes a method practiced during 2018–2019; this current candidate advances the runnable exemplar's recovery behavior while preserving capture-format compatibility.

technicalVeracity.basis: Focused tests exercise normalization, negation retention, review standing, deterministic ordering and rendering, and the shared directory/file transition through pre-effect and post-effect events at prior movement, activation, successor retention, restoration, staged retention, typed recovery, and post-acceptance cleanup in the resolved environment.

execution.runtime: Python >=3.12,<3.13; local OCR additionally requires a Tesseract executable

commands.name: run
commands.establishes: Produces 0.1.1 ordered term evidence, a seeded word-cloud orientation image, and digest-bearing render metadata from a compatible 0.1.0 reviewed synthetic capture.

commands.name: test
commands.establishes: Exercises deterministic analysis and the shared cooperative single-writer transition, including pre-effect and post-effect Python events, original-event propagation, typed observed-state recovery, staged retention, and post-acceptance retirement behavior.

commands.name: lint
commands.establishes: Returns focused Python syntax, import, correctness, modernization, and maintainability diagnostics for the analysis and promotion modules.

environmentNotes: The ordinary analysis and test route consumes reviewed text and does not require Tesseract.
Artifact and emitted output workflow identity is 0.1.1; coherent existing and newly collected OCR captures retain captureVersion 0.1.0.
Explicit replacement can receive an owned 0.1.0 analysis-output sentinel as a migration input; the successor emits a 0.1.1 sentinel.
Promotion assumes one cooperative writer and a trusted parent directory for the transition interval.
Repeated-render byte equality is asserted within one resolved environment; cross-platform image-library differences remain an observation boundary.

reviewQuestions: Can a reviewer inspect what OCR produced before weighting begins?
Do directory and capture replacement share one semantic transition?
Which original Python event is propagated after successful restoration?
Did an operation event arrive before or after its filesystem effect?
Which causes and coordinates remain available when restoration also stops?
Which future mechanism would establish a broader writer, reader, platform, or durability guarantee?
decisionRules: Treat captured OCR as observed input and keep human review standing visible through analysis.
Stage a complete sibling result and require explicit authority plus an owned 0.1.0 migration or 0.1.1 current sentinel before moving an accepted target.
Use the shared transition while one cooperative writer owns a trusted parent directory.
Observe the named coordinates after every operation event, reconcile pre-effect and post-effect states, and retain every cause, coordinate, phase, and occupancy when recovery stops.
Accept the successor before carrier-specific retirement and describe recursive cleanup results by the material actually observed.

semanticMarkers.meaning: Source-digested capture, visible negation, ordered evidence, deterministic rendering, and one typed promotion transition for directory and file carriers.
Carrier-specific replacement paths that discard staged recovery material or replace the event that first interrupted promotion.

Explicit authority, complete sibling staging, rename-effect reconciliation, original-event propagation, typed observed-state recovery, and post-acceptance retirement keep recovery coordinates legible.

instructionYields.instruction: Separate environment-observed collection from deterministic analysis and route file and directory replacement through one semantic transition.
Inspect capture version, workflow version, accepted target, staged successor, prior coordinate, and typed causes as distinct state.
Classify each operation event from observed coordinates, restore the accepted target while cleanup can execute, and retain every event, phase, coordinate, and occupancy when recovery stops.

practice.codeExemplarGranularity: One self-contained collection-and-analysis workflow, one shared file/directory promotion module, compatible synthetic captures, and focused transition tests.
practice.complexityAndAllocation: Text normalization and sparse TF-IDF fitting remain the main analysis work. A finite promotion transition, named-coordinate observations, and a narrow operation adapter isolate recovery behavior from carrier cleanup and incidental path lookup counts.

boundaries.evidence: Focused tests establish deterministic analysis and injected pre-effect and post-effect Python-event recovery states on real temporary filesystems in the resolved environment. Static symbolic-link and ownership checks are momentary observations within the trusted-parent model; they are not TOCTOU protection.
boundaries.trust: The fixture is realistic synthetic material, the historical method is participant-account-supported, and replacement assumes one cooperative writer with a trusted parent directory. Another process with equal parent-directory authority remains outside this boundary.
boundaries.transfer: A receiver selects its corpus, review policy, parent-directory authority, filesystem and platform contract, writer and reader model, and durability requirement. Participating POSIX coordination, process or host restart durability, descriptor/no-follow hardening, same-authority resistance, complete old-or-new reader visibility, and Windows handle parity each retain a distinct future probe.

failureModes: Missing analysis dependencies stop before output staging.
Malformed captures and output ownership outside the explicit 0.1.0 migration or 0.1.1 current contract stop before promotion.
An operation event can arrive before or after its rename effect; the transition classifies the observed staged, target, and prior coordinates before recovery continues.
A recovery operation can also receive an event, yielding either a restored prior plus attached post-effect event or a typed state for re-entry.
Post-acceptance directory retirement can partially complete before reporting an error.
recoveryMoves: Resolve the committed lock or repair the capture, then rerun the same candidate command.
Choose a new target or grant explicit --replace authority only for an owned 0.1.0 migration input or 0.1.1 current output.
After successful reconciliation, inspect the retained stage, original propagated event, and any attached post-effect recovery events.
On PromotionRecoveryError, inspect primary_error, recovery_errors, phase, state, staged, target, and prior before selecting a recovery move.
After a retirement warning, treat the successor as accepted and inspect the named remaining material before cleanup continues.
